terms.definition: A long DNA molecule carrying many genes, found in the nucleus. Body cells have 23 pairs.
terms.examiner: Chromosomes come in pairs: one from each parent.

terms.definition: The series of stages in which a cell grows, copies its DNA and sub-cellular structures, then divides by mitosis into two identical cells.
terms.examiner: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells.

terms.definition: Cell division that produces two genetically identical cells; used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.
terms.examiner: One set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell, then the cytoplasm and membrane divide.

terms.definition: The process by which a cell becomes specialised for a particular job.
terms.examiner: Most animal cells differentiate early on; many plant cells can differentiate throughout life.

terms.definition: An undifferentiated cell that can divide to make more stem cells and differentiate into some or many types of cell.
terms.examiner: Embryonic stem cells can become most cell types; adult bone marrow stem cells only some.

terms.definition: Plant tissue at the tips of roots and shoots where cells divide; it can differentiate into any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
terms.examiner: Used to make clones of rare plants or crops quickly and cheaply.

terms.definition: Making an embryo with the same genes as the patient so that its stem cells are not rejected by the patient's immune system.
terms.examiner: Ethical objections and the risk of transferring a viral infection are common evaluation points.
